Indonesia's volcanic eruptions, in order.Samalas (Rinjani), Lombok: Its 1257 eruption was among the biggest in 10,000 years, and its location was found by studying volcanic debris in ice cores.
Indonesia's volcanic eruptions, in order.Tambora: Its 1815 eruption caused 'the year without a summer' in 1816, which may have inspired Frankenstein.
Indonesia's volcanic eruptions, in order.Krakatoa: The 1883 blast was heard about 4,800 km away, and its tsunamis killed over 36,000 people.
Indonesia's volcanic eruptions, in order.Kelud: Mudflows from the 1919 eruption killed about 5,000 people in East Java, prompting Dutch-built drainage tunnels.
Indonesia's volcanic eruptions, in order.Agung, Bali: Bali's holiest mountain erupted in 1963, killing over a thousand people.
Indonesia's volcanic eruptions, in order.Galunggung: The 1982 eruption sent ash into British Airways Flight 9, which lost all four engines but restarted them.
Indonesia's volcanic eruptions, in order.Merapi: Java's most active volcano erupted in 2010, killing over 350, including its spiritual caretaker Mbah Maridjan.
Indonesia's volcanic eruptions, in order.Anak Krakatau collapse: A flank collapse into the sea triggered a tsunami in the Sunda Strait, killing over 400 people.
Indonesia's volcanic eruptions, in order.Semeru: Java's tallest volcano, about 3,676 m, erupted in December 2021 with deadly pyroclastic flows.
Indonesia's volcanic eruptions, in order.Marapi, Sumatra: The December 2023 eruption killed over 20 hikers on the mountain's slopes.

Surahs of the Qur'an, in order.Al-Fatiha: The opening chapter has just seven verses and is recited in every Muslim prayer, which is why it is often called the Opening.
Surahs of the Qur'an, in order.Al-Baqarah: At 286 verses it is the longest surah, named after the heifer in a story about Moses and the Israelites.
Surahs of the Qur'an, in order.Al Imran: The title means 'Family of Imran', a reference to the family of Mary, mother of Jesus, which the surah discusses at length.
Surahs of the Qur'an, in order.Yusuf: Unusually, the whole story of the prophet Joseph is told in this one surah, from his dream and jealous brothers to his rise in Egypt.
Surahs of the Qur'an, in order.Al-Kahf: Many Muslims read it on Fridays; it includes the tale of the Sleepers of the Cave, youths who slept for centuries.
Surahs of the Qur'an, in order.Maryam: Named for Mary, it is the only chapter named after a woman, and she is the only woman named in the Qur'an.
Surahs of the Qur'an, in order.Ya-Sin: Tradition calls it the heart of the Qur'an, and it is often recited for the dying and at gatherings of remembrance.
Surahs of the Qur'an, in order.Ar-Rahman: It repeats the refrain 'Which of your Lord's favours will you deny?' 31 times, addressed to both humans and jinn.
Surahs of the Qur'an, in order.Al-Ikhlas: Just four verses on the oneness of God, yet tradition says reciting it equals a third of the Qur'an in merit.
Surahs of the Qur'an, in order.An-Nas: The final chapter, titled 'Mankind', is a short prayer seeking refuge in God from whispering evil, recited at bedtime by many.

Classical hits, by when they were first.Vivaldi's Four Seasons: Each concerto is paired with a sonnet, and the violins imitate birdsong and storms.
Classical hits, by when they were first.Handel's Messiah: Audiences traditionally stand for its Hallelujah chorus, supposedly because King George II once rose.
Classical hits, by when they were first.Eine kleine Nachtmusik: The title means 'a little night music'; Mozart wrote it in Vienna but it was not published until after his death.
Classical hits, by when they were first.Beethoven's Fifth Symphony: Famous four-note opening; it premiered in a freezing four-hour concert.
Classical hits, by when they were first.Beethoven's Ninth (Ode to Joy): Beethoven was almost completely deaf when he wrote the first symphony to include choral voices.
Classical hits, by when they were first.The Blue Danube: Johann Strauss II's waltz was originally choral; it became the theme of 2001: A Space Odyssey.
Classical hits, by when they were first.Holst's The Planets: Holst's suite omits Earth and Pluto, which was not discovered until 1930.
Classical hits, by when they were first.Rhapsody in Blue: Gershwin wrote it in about five weeks; it opens with a clarinet glissando.
Classical hits, by when they were first.Ravel's Boléro: One melody repeats over a steady snare drum, getting louder; Ravel called it an orchestral experiment.
Classical hits, by when they were first.Cage's 4′33″: Performers do not play a single note; the audience hears the ambient sounds of the room.

Landlocked countries by area.Vatican City: The smallest sovereign state in the world is about the size of a city park, entirely surrounded by Rome.
Landlocked countries by area.Luxembourg: It is the world's only remaining grand duchy, and one of the wealthiest countries per person.
Landlocked countries by area.Switzerland: Despite having no coast, it runs a merchant fleet of ships flying the Swiss flag.
Landlocked countries by area.Hungary: The Danube flows through its capital Budapest, and Lake Balaton is the largest lake in Central Europe.
Landlocked countries by area.Laos: Its former name, Lan Xang, meant a million elephants; the Mekong forms much of its western border.
Landlocked countries by area.Paraguay: It has two official languages, Spanish and Guarani, and Guarani is spoken by most of its people.
Landlocked countries by area.South Sudan: It is the world's newest country, having gained independence from Sudan in 2011.
Landlocked countries by area.Zambia: Part of Victoria Falls is here; locals call the falls Mosi-oa-Tunya, which means the smoke that thunders.
Landlocked countries by area.Bolivia: It has two capitals, La Paz and Sucre, and it lost its entire coastline to Chile in the War of the Pacific.
Landlocked countries by area.Chad: Lake Chad, on its border, has shrunk to a fraction of its 1960s size, one of the most dramatic ecological changes on Earth.

Daring medical firsts.Lamb's blood transfused to man: The French doctor Jean-Baptiste Denis's experiment of transfusing lamb blood into a boy was followed by deaths that led to bans.
Daring medical firsts.Smallpox vaccine: Edward Jenner noticed milkmaids with cowpox escaped smallpox, and vaccine comes from vacca, Latin for cow.
Daring medical firsts.Ether anesthesia: Before ether, surgeons raced to finish operations in minutes while patients were held down.
Daring medical firsts.First X-ray image: Wilhelm Rontgen X-rayed his wife Anna's hand, showing bones and her ring, and she reportedly said she had seen her death.
Daring medical firsts.Human heart transplant: Christiaan Barnard performed it in Cape Town on Louis Washkansky, who lived 18 days.
Daring medical firsts.Monkey head transplant: Robert White's experiment linked a monkey's head to another body; it survived for days but was paralysed, and remains deeply controversial.
Daring medical firsts.Test-tube baby: Louise Brown, born in England in July 1978, was the first IVF baby, and pioneer Robert Edwards won a 2010 Nobel Prize.
Daring medical firsts.Hand transplant: A first lasting hand transplant took place in Lyon, France, and recipients must take anti-rejection drugs for life.
Daring medical firsts.Face transplant: Isabelle Dinoire received the first partial one in Amiens, France, after a dog attack.
Daring medical firsts.Pig heart into a human: David Bennett received a genetically modified pig heart in Maryland and survived about two months.

Minimum aging required for these cheeses.Fresh mozzarella: This stretched-curd cheese is traditionally made from water buffalo milk in Campania and eaten within days.
Minimum aging required for these cheeses.Camembert de Normandie: Its protected version must be made with raw milk in Normandy, whereas most industrial Camembert uses pasteurised milk.
Minimum aging required for these cheeses.Brie de Meaux: It was declared 'king of cheeses' at the 1815 Congress of Vienna, where diplomats voted on the best cheese.
Minimum aging required for these cheeses.Feta: The name feta is protected for Greece, where it's made from sheep's milk, with up to 30% goat milk allowed.
Minimum aging required for these cheeses.Roquefort: It ripens in the natural caves of Combalou, where the mould Penicillium roquefortii grows.
Minimum aging required for these cheeses.Comté: Made in the Jura from Montbéliarde cows, its wheels weigh around 40 kg, and a single wheel takes about 400 litres of milk.
Minimum aging required for these cheeses.Gruyère AOP: This Swiss cheese has only tiny holes, unlike Emmental, and its name is protected by AOP rules from its home region.
Minimum aging required for these cheeses.Grana Padano: The name grana refers to its grainy texture, and it's a milder, cheaper cousin of Parmesan made across northern Italy.
Minimum aging required for these cheeses.Parmigiano Reggiano: Wheels weigh about 40 kg and are aged on wooden shelves, with a dotted rind.
Minimum aging required for these cheeses.Grana Padano Riserva: The long ageing earns it a premium over standard Grana Padano, with a harder, more crystalline texture and stronger flavour.

Extreme human endurance, by duration.Longest Moon walk (Apollo 17): On Apollo 17, Cernan and Schmitt drove the rover and brought back about 110 kilograms of samples on the Moon's longest outing.
Extreme human endurance, by duration.Longest kiss record: A Thai couple took the title in 2013, in a competition where the pair had to stay locked together, with only short breaks.
Extreme human endurance, by duration.Randy Gardner stays awake: The San Diego teenager stayed up for 11 days in 1964 for a science fair project, and suffered hallucinations and memory trouble.
Extreme human endurance, by duration.Angus Barbieri's fast: Under medical supervision, the Scottish man lived on vitamins and water, and lost about 125 kilograms.
Extreme human endurance, by duration.Polyakov's stay in space: The cosmonaut holds the record for the longest single spaceflight, on Mir in 1994-95, and came back able to walk.
Extreme human endurance, by duration.Donna Griffiths's sneezing fit: A British schoolgirl sneezed an estimated million times in her first year, and the fit stopped abruptly after 976 days.
Extreme human endurance, by duration.Irom Sharmila's hunger strike: The Manipuri activist fasted for 16 years to protest against a law giving soldiers special powers, and was force-fed through a nose tube.
Extreme human endurance, by duration.Elaine Esposito's coma: She fell into a coma after an operation at age six, and never woke, dying at 43 after the longest recorded coma.
Extreme human endurance, by duration.Charles Osborne's hiccups: An Iowa farmer started hiccuping after falling while he was weighing a hog, and the hiccups stopped the year before he died.
Extreme human endurance, by duration.Jeanne Calment's life: She holds the longest verified human lifespan, and she met Vincent van Gogh as a girl in her father's shop in Arles.

Kitchen temperatures.Refrigerator: Fridges should stay below about 5 degrees to slow the growth of bacteria, which multiply fast in warm kitchens.
Kitchen temperatures.Butter melts: It melts a little below body temperature, which is why a pat of it dissolves so easily in your mouth.
Kitchen temperatures.Medium-rare steak, inside: This is the classic doneness for a good steak, with a warm red center that stays juicy.
Kitchen temperatures.Safely cooked chicken: It's the safe internal temperature health authorities recommend for chicken, high enough to kill salmonella.
Kitchen temperatures.Water boils: Water boils at lower temperatures at altitude, so in Denver it boils at about 95 degrees and pasta takes longer.
Kitchen temperatures.Sugar at soft-ball stage: At this stage of cooking sugar syrup, a drop in cold water forms a soft ball, and you can make fudge and fondant.
Kitchen temperatures.Sugar at hard-crack stage: Toffee and brittle are made at this stage, when a drop of syrup in cold water turns brittle and snaps.
Kitchen temperatures.Deep-frying oil: Hot oil crisps food because surface water instantly flashes to steam, leaving a dry, golden crust.
Kitchen temperatures.Home oven at max: A typical home oven tops out around 500 degrees Fahrenheit, far below what a wood-fired oven reaches.
Kitchen temperatures.Neapolitan pizza oven: It cooks a pizza in about 60 to 90 seconds, which is why the crust blisters and the center stays soft.

Telescopes by mirror or dish diameter.Spitzer Space Telescope: The infrared observatory, active until 2020, trailed Earth around the Sun rather than orbiting it.
Telescopes by mirror or dish diameter.Hubble Space Telescope: Launched in 1990 with a flawed mirror, it was fixed by astronauts in 1993 using corrective optics.
Telescopes by mirror or dish diameter.Herschel Space Observatory: The largest infrared telescope launched, it studied star birth and ran out of coolant in 2013.
Telescopes by mirror or dish diameter.Hale Telescope (Palomar): It was the world's largest telescope for decades, and it's named after George Ellery Hale.
Telescopes by mirror or dish diameter.James Webb Space Telescope: Its golden mirror has 18 hexagonal segments, and it sits about 1.5 million km from Earth.
Telescopes by mirror or dish diameter.Keck: Twin telescopes on Mauna Kea, Hawaii, each with a mirror made of 36 hexagonal segments.
Telescopes by mirror or dish diameter.Giant Magellan Telescope: Under construction in Chile, it will combine seven giant mirrors into one.
Telescopes by mirror or dish diameter.Extremely Large Telescope: Being built in Chile's Atacama Desert, its mirror will be made of nearly 800 hexagonal segments.
Telescopes by mirror or dish diameter.Arecibo: Built into a natural sinkhole in Puerto Rico, it collapsed in 2020 and starred in GoldenEye and Contact.
Telescopes by mirror or dish diameter.FAST (China): Nicknamed Tianyan, the 'Eye of Heaven', in Guizhou, China, it is the largest single-dish radio telescope.

Debut years of these video game heroes.Pac-Man: Pac-Man's shape reportedly came from a pizza with a slice missing, and it became one of the highest-earning arcade games ever.
Debut years of these video game heroes.Mario: Mario first appeared as Jumpman in Donkey Kong, and he is a plumber by trade.
Debut years of these video game heroes.Link: Link is the silent hero of The Legend of Zelda, and he's usually the one saving the princess named in the title.
Debut years of these video game heroes.Mega Man: Capcom's blue robot hero was inspired by Astro Boy and gains the powers of defeated bosses.
Debut years of these video game heroes.Sonic: Sega created this blue hedgehog to rival Mario, and he can run faster than sound.
Debut years of these video game heroes.Kirby: The pink puffball can inhale enemies and copy their powers, and he was created by Masahiro Sakurai.
Debut years of these video game heroes.Lara Croft: The archaeologist adventurer from Tomb Raider was one of the first video game characters to become a global star.
Debut years of these video game heroes.Master Chief: John-117, known as Master Chief, is a Spartan super-soldier in the Halo series, and his face is never shown behind the visor.
Debut years of these video game heroes.Kratos: The Greek god of war from the PlayStation series has a 2018 reboot set in a Norse world.
Debut years of these video game heroes.Steve (Minecraft): Steve is the default skin in Minecraft, a blocky character, and he has become a mascot in his own right.

Lesser-known Greek letters, in alphabet.Β Beta: Beta and alpha together gave us the word 'alphabet', and 'beta' is now the name for the second, trial version of software.
Lesser-known Greek letters, in alphabet.Δ Delta: Its triangle shape gave river deltas their name, after Herodotus noticed the Nile's mouth looked like the letter.
Lesser-known Greek letters, in alphabet.Ζ Zeta: The Riemann zeta function, a famous mathematical tool, is closely tied to the pattern of the prime numbers.
Lesser-known Greek letters, in alphabet.Ι Iota: It is the smallest Greek letter, which is why 'not one iota' means not even a tiny bit.
Lesser-known Greek letters, in alphabet.Κ Kappa: Phi Beta Kappa, founded in 1776, is America's oldest academic honor society, and its name comes from three Greek letters.
Lesser-known Greek letters, in alphabet.Μ Mu: Scientists use it for the prefix 'micro', one millionth, and also for the muon, a heavy cousin of the electron.
Lesser-known Greek letters, in alphabet.Ξ Xi: Pronounced 'ksee', it names a family of heavy subatomic particles, and also appears in a function in number theory.
Lesser-known Greek letters, in alphabet.Ρ Rho: Physicists use it for density, and statisticians for a correlation coefficient. In Greek it is pronounced 'roh'.
Lesser-known Greek letters, in alphabet.Τ Tau: Some mathematicians promote tau as the circle constant 2π, about 6.28, and celebrate Tau Day each June 28.
Lesser-known Greek letters, in alphabet.Ψ Psi: Shaped like Poseidon's trident, it stands for psychology, and also for the wave function in quantum mechanics.

Milestones in the Prophet Muhammad's lif.Born in Mecca: Muhammad was born in Mecca into the Quraysh tribe, and he was orphaned young, raised first by his grandfather and then by his uncle Abu Talib.
Milestones in the Prophet Muhammad's lif.Marries Khadija: His first wife was a successful merchant 15 years his senior, and she supported him through the early years of his mission.
Milestones in the Prophet Muhammad's lif.First revelation: He received the first verses of the Quran in a cave on Mount Hira, where he went to meditate, and the angel Gabriel appeared to him.
Milestones in the Prophet Muhammad's lif.Hijra to Medina: The migration to Medina marks Year 1 of the Islamic calendar, and not his birth or the first revelation.
Milestones in the Prophet Muhammad's lif.Battle of Badr: This first major battle took place near wells in the desert, where a smaller Muslim force defeated a larger Meccan army.
Milestones in the Prophet Muhammad's lif.Battle of Uhud: The battle was fought near a mountain north of Medina, and the Muslims were at first winning until archers left their posts.
Milestones in the Prophet Muhammad's lif.Battle of the Trench: Muslims dug a trench around Medina, an idea attributed to the Persian Salman, to defend against a large besieging force.
Milestones in the Prophet Muhammad's lif.Treaty of Hudaybiyyah: This treaty was a ten-year truce with Mecca, which seemed to favour the Quraysh, though it allowed the Muslims to make a pilgrimage the next year.
Milestones in the Prophet Muhammad's lif.Conquest of Mecca: Muhammad returned to his home city largely without bloodshed, and he cleared the Kaaba of idols.
Milestones in the Prophet Muhammad's lif.Death in Medina: He died in the home of his wife Aisha and was buried there, and the Prophet's Mosque now stands over the site.

Weather, from droplets to giant swirls.Fog droplet: Fog is just a cloud at ground level, with droplets so light they hang in the air.
Weather, from droplets to giant swirls.Drizzle drop: Drizzle falls from low, thin clouds in drops under about half a millimeter.
Weather, from droplets to giant swirls.Raindrop: Small raindrops are spheres, and big ones flatten like hamburger buns, never the teardrop shape of drawings.
Weather, from droplets to giant swirls.Lightning channel: The channel is thin but heats the air to about 30,000 °C, and that blast causes thunder.
Weather, from droplets to giant swirls.Golf-ball hailstone: Hailstones grow by cycling up and down in updrafts, adding layers like an onion.
Weather, from droplets to giant swirls.Dust devil: These form on hot sunny days, not from storms, and Mars has them too.
Weather, from droplets to giant swirls.Tornado: The strongest tornadoes exceed 400 km/h, with winds among the fastest on Earth.
Weather, from droplets to giant swirls.Thunderstorm cell: Around 2,000 thunderstorms are active worldwide at any moment.
Weather, from droplets to giant swirls.Hurricane: The same storm is called a typhoon or cyclone depending on the ocean, and its eye is calm.
Weather, from droplets to giant swirls.Polar vortex: It's a band of cold low pressure over the poles, and when it weakens, cold air spills south.

Power output, from LED to the Sun.LED light bulb: An LED turns far more of its electricity into light than an old incandescent bulb, which wasted most of its power as heat.
Power output, from LED to the Sun.Human brain: The brain is about 2 percent of body weight but uses roughly 20 percent of its energy, about the draw of a dim light bulb.
Power output, from LED to the Sun.Human body at rest: A resting person gives off about as much heat as a 100-watt bulb, which is why a crowded room quickly warms up.
Power output, from LED to the Sun.Microwave oven: Microwaves heat food with radio waves that make water molecules jiggle; the first commercial model, Raytheon's Radarange, stood as tall as a person.
Power output, from LED to the Sun.Electric kettle: When a popular British TV show ends, millions of kettles switch on together, causing a surge in grid demand known as TV pickup.
Power output, from LED to the Sun.Family car engine: This is about 134 horsepower, a unit James Watt invented to show steam-engine buyers how many horses an engine could replace.
Power output, from LED to the Sun.Wind turbine: No turbine can capture more than about 59 percent of the wind's energy, a limit known as the Betz limit.
Power output, from LED to the Sun.Nuclear reactor: Fuel pellets the size of a fingertip power a reactor, and one large reactor can supply electricity to hundreds of thousands of homes.
Power output, from LED to the Sun.Lightning bolt (peak): A bolt heats the air around it to about 30,000 °C, several times hotter than the surface of the Sun, causing thunder.
Power output, from LED to the Sun.The Sun: The Sun converts roughly four million tonnes of matter into energy every second, yet has fuel for billions more years.

Compass bearings.North: True north and magnetic north differ, and the magnetic pole slowly wanders, so a compass needle points close to, but not at, the North Pole.
Compass bearings.North-northeast: This is one of the 16 points of the traditional compass rose, each 22.5 degrees from the next, and sailors learned to recite them.
Compass bearings.Northeast: Northeast is an intercardinal direction, halfway between north and east, which is why it's marked at 45 degrees.
Compass bearings.East: To orient originally meant to face east, toward the rising Sun, and many old maps put east at the top.
Compass bearings.Southeast: Bearings are measured clockwise from north, which is why southeast sits at 135 degrees, halfway between east and south.
Compass bearings.South: In the Southern Hemisphere, extending the Southern Cross's long axis about four and a half times points close to due south.
Compass bearings.Southwest: Southwesterly winds dominate western Europe, which is a major reason Britain's weather is mild and wet.
Compass bearings.West-southwest: Reciting all 32 points of the compass in order is called boxing the compass, a skill once required of sailors.
Compass bearings.West: The Sun rises and sets due east and west only at the equinoxes; at other times it is north or south of those points.
Compass bearings.Northwest: The Northwest Passage, sought for centuries as a sea route to Asia, runs through Arctic Canada.

Area: from tiny state to continent.Vatican City: The smallest sovereign state has its own post office, radio station and Swiss Guard.
Area: from tiny state to continent.Monaco: Monaco is the world's most densely populated country, and its Grand Prix runs on city streets.
Area: from tiny state to continent.Central Park: Designed by Olmsted and Vaux, it is bigger than the whole country of Monaco.
Area: from tiny state to continent.Manhattan: The street grid was laid out in 1811, and legend says Dutch settlers bought the island for trinkets, which is disputed.
Area: from tiny state to continent.Walt Disney World resort: Roughly the size of San Francisco, it has four theme parks and its own bus system.
Area: from tiny state to continent.Singapore: It has grown by about a quarter through land reclamation since independence.
Area: from tiny state to continent.Luxembourg: The world's only remaining grand duchy, with three official languages.
Area: from tiny state to continent.Wales: Often used as a yardstick: 'the size of Wales' is the stock comparison for forest loss.
Area: from tiny state to continent.Texas: Larger than France, it was an independent republic from 1836 to 1845.
Area: from tiny state to continent.Australia: It is both a country and a continent, slightly smaller than the 48 contiguous US states.

Units of speed.1 furlong per fortnight: It is a joke unit, and a garden snail moves far faster; it appears in the tongue-in-cheek FFF system of units.
Units of speed.1 inch per second: Engineers use it for slow things, like paper feeding through a printer or a 3D printer's head.
Units of speed.1 km/h: The metric road-sign unit; for scale, Usain Bolt's peak sprint speed is about 44 of them.
Units of speed.1 foot per second: Used in ballistics and fluid flow; an ordinary walking pace is about four or five of them.
Units of speed.1 mph: Still used on UK and US roads, with the UK the main European country to keep miles on its signs.
Units of speed.1 knot: One nautical mile per hour; the name comes from knots tied along a ship's log line to measure speed.
Units of speed.1 m/s: The standard SI unit of speed, used in science for everything from wind to falling objects.
Units of speed.Mach 1 at sea level: It varies with temperature and is slower at altitude; Chuck Yeager first broke it in a rocket plane in 1947.
Units of speed.1 km/s: Spacecraft speeds are quoted this way; the International Space Station orbits at about 7.7 km/s.
Units of speed.Speed of light: Nothing with mass can reach it, and sunlight takes about eight minutes to cross the gap to Earth.

When these fragrances launched.Chanel No. 5: Ernest Beaux's creation was the first famous fragrance to use aldehydes in large amounts, and Marilyn Monroe famously said she wore it to bed.
When these fragrances launched.Shalimar (Guerlain): Shalimar was named after the Mughal gardens in Lahore, which Shah Jahan built for his wife, and it is considered the first oriental fragrance.
When these fragrances launched.Old Spice: Old Spice began as a women's line, and its sailor-themed ads helped make it an American classic.
When these fragrances launched.Miss Dior: Christian Dior's first perfume was named after his sister Catherine, a French Resistance member who survived a concentration camp.
When these fragrances launched.Brut: Brut was promoted by boxer Muhammad Ali and soccer star Henry Cooper, and it made men's cologne a mass-market product.
When these fragrances launched.Opium (YSL): Opium caused uproar over its name, which protestors said glamorized drugs, but it became a bestseller.
When these fragrances launched.Drakkar Noir: The fragrance by Guy Laroche, in a sleek black bottle, became popular as a sporty scent in the 1980s.
When these fragrances launched.CK One: Calvin Klein's unisex scent was a hit, and its minimalist marketing helped reshape fragrance as something to share.
When these fragrances launched.Acqua di Giò: Giorgio Armani's aquatic scent was named after the island of Pantelleria and Capri, and it started the aquatic fragrance trend.
When these fragrances launched.Dior Sauvage: Sauvage, with Johnny Depp as the face, became one of the best-selling men's fragrances, and its name means wild in French.

When these bands were formed.The Rolling Stones: They took their name from the Muddy Waters song 'Rollin' Stone' and have played for six decades.
When these bands were formed.Pink Floyd: Syd Barrett named it after two blues musicians, Pink Anderson and Floyd Council.
When these bands were formed.Led Zeppelin: The name may come from a joke that a band would 'go over like a lead balloon', with the spelling changed to avoid mispronunciation.
When these bands were formed.Queen: Guitarist Brian May completed an astrophysics PhD in 2007, decades after leaving his studies to join the band.
When these bands were formed.Ramones: All four took the stage surname Ramone, though none were related, and they played fast, short songs at New York's CBGB.
When these bands were formed.U2: Larry Mullen put up a note on a school notice board in Dublin looking for bandmates, and the rest answered.
When these bands were formed.Metallica: Lars Ulrich put an ad in a Los Angeles paper, and James Hetfield answered it.
When these bands were formed.Oasis: Noel Gallagher joined his younger brother Liam's band and became its songwriter, helping launch Britpop's biggest rivalry.
When these bands were formed.Foo Fighters: Dave Grohl played nearly every instrument on the debut, after Nirvana ended, and the name comes from World War II slang for UFOs.
When these bands were formed.Arctic Monkeys: Their debut became the fastest-selling debut album in UK history, boosted by fans sharing songs online, notably on MySpace.

French numbers, including the tricky one.onze: Unlike its English cousin, 'onze' does not take 'l'' before it, so you say 'le onze'.
French numbers, including the tricky one.seize: After seize, French gets 'dix-sept', literally ten-seven, rather than a new word.
French numbers, including the tricky one.vingt: The final consonant is silent on its own, but it comes back in a liaison, as in 'vingt ans'.
French numbers, including the tricky one.trente: It comes from the Latin triginta, and the French tens up to sixty follow a regular pattern.
French numbers, including the tricky one.cinquante: It descends from the Latin quinquaginta, and its stem is cinq, the word for five.
French numbers, including the tricky one.soixante-dix: It literally means sixty-ten, while in Belgium and Switzerland people say 'septante'.
French numbers, including the tricky one.quatre-vingts: It literally means four twenties, a trace of ancient base-20 counting, and Switzerland uses 'huitante' in some regions.
French numbers, including the tricky one.quatre-vingt-dix: It is literally four twenties ten, and Belgium and Switzerland use 'nonante'.
French numbers, including the tricky one.cent: It comes from the Latin centum, which also gives us 'percent' and 'century'.
French numbers, including the tricky one.mille: English 'mile' comes from the Latin 'mille passus', or a thousand paces.

The Lord of the Rings, in story order.Bilbo's farewell party: The 111th birthday of Bilbo and 33rd of Frodo; Bilbo vanishes with the Ring in front of his guests.
The Lord of the Rings, in story order.Frodo stabbed on Weathertop: The Witch-king wounds Frodo with a Morgul blade, a shard of which works toward his heart.
The Lord of the Rings, in story order.The Council of Elrond: The council gathers in Rivendell and forms the Fellowship of nine walkers to oppose the Nine Riders.
The Lord of the Rings, in story order.Gandalf falls in Moria: He fights the Balrog on the Bridge of Khazad-dum and later returns as Gandalf the White.
The Lord of the Rings, in story order.Boromir dies: He dies defending Merry and Pippin from Uruk-hai, after trying to take the Ring from Frodo.
The Lord of the Rings, in story order.Battle of Helm's Deep: Theoden's stronghold in Rohan holds out against Saruman's army until Gandalf arrives at dawn.
The Lord of the Rings, in story order.Shelob attacks Frodo: The giant spider stings Frodo at Cirith Ungol; Sam later wields the Phial of Galadriel against her.
The Lord of the Rings, in story order.Battle of the Pelennor Fields: The great battle before Minas Tirith, where Eowyn slays the Witch-king of Angmar.
The Lord of the Rings, in story order.The Ring is destroyed: Gollum bites off Frodo's finger and falls into Mount Doom; fans mark March 25 as Tolkien Reading Day.
The Lord of the Rings, in story order.The Scouring of the Shire: The hobbits return to a Shire ruled by Saruman, a final conflict the Peter Jackson films left out.

Rome before the emperors, in order.Rome founded (legend): Rome's founding legend gives April 21, 753 BC as its birthday. Romans celebrated it with a festival long after.
Rome before the emperors, in order.Republic founded: The Romans threw out the last king, Tarquin, and instead elected two consuls each year. The idea was that no one could rule alone.
Rome before the emperors, in order.Gauls sack Rome: Legend says sacred geese on the Capitoline Hill raised the alarm when Gauls crept up. The defeated Romans paid a ransom in gold.
Rome before the emperors, in order.Pyrrhus wins at Heraclea: Pyrrhus won at Heraclea using war elephants, which Romans had never seen. He lost so many men that "Pyrrhic victory" entered the language.
Rome before the emperors, in order.First Punic War begins: Rome and Carthage fought over Sicily for 23 years. Rome built a navy from scratch, copying a captured Carthaginian ship.
Rome before the emperors, in order.Hannibal crosses the Alps: Hannibal crossed the Alps with elephants, and lost many of them to cold and cliffs. He still reached Italy and kept winning for years.
Rome before the emperors, in order.Carthage destroyed: The Romans destroyed Carthage after a long siege. Cato the Elder ended every speech with "Carthage must be destroyed."
Rome before the emperors, in order.Spartacus' revolt: The gladiator Spartacus led an army of escaped slaves that beat several Roman forces. Crassus crushed it, crucifying thousands along the Appian Way.
Rome before the emperors, in order.Caesar crosses the Rubicon: Caesar crossed this small river with his army, defying the Senate, and said "the die is cast." It started a civil war.
Rome before the emperors, in order.Caesar assassinated: Senators stabbed Caesar on the Ides of March, around 23 times. Their plot to save the Republic instead ended it.

Chat and messaging apps by launch.IRC: Finnish student Jarkko Oikarinen wrote it, and it still hosts chat channels, decades on.
Chat and messaging apps by launch.ICQ: Its name sounds like 'I seek you'; this Israeli-made messenger introduced the buddy list and was sold to AOL for about 400 million dollars.
Chat and messaging apps by launch.AIM: AOL Instant Messenger's door-creak sound and away messages defined teenage chatting until it shut down in 2017.
Chat and messaging apps by launch.Yahoo! Messenger: It began as Yahoo! Pager and offered 'buzz' alerts; Yahoo shut the service down in 2018.
Chat and messaging apps by launch.MSN Messenger: Its 'nudge' shook your friend's window; Microsoft retired it in 2013, steering users toward Skype.
Chat and messaging apps by launch.BlackBerry Messenger: BlackBerry's PIN-based chat was a status symbol for 2000s business users; the consumer app closed in 2019.
Chat and messaging apps by launch.iMessage: Apple's blue-bubble service arrived with iOS 5, while a green bubble marks an ordinary SMS text.
Chat and messaging apps by launch.Telegram: Founded by the Russian brothers Pavel and Nikolai Durov, it is known for huge channels and cloud-synced chats.
Chat and messaging apps by launch.Slack: It grew out of Tiny Speck, a failed video game company; its name is said to stand for 'searchable log of all conversation and knowledge'.
Chat and messaging apps by launch.Microsoft Teams: Microsoft built it to compete with Slack, and usage surged when offices went remote in 2020.

California earthquakes, in order.Fort Tejon: One of California's most powerful quakes, around magnitude 7.9, ruptured the San Andreas for about 350 km, but few people lived nearby.
California earthquakes, in order.San Francisco: It killed about 3,000 people and mostly burned the city, and it inspired the theory that rocks snap back along faults.
California earthquakes, in order.Long Beach: Its collapsing schools led to the Field Act, which required earthquake-resistant school construction.
California earthquakes, in order.Kern County: At magnitude 7.3, it was the biggest California quake since 1906 when it struck.
California earthquakes, in order.San Fernando (Sylmar): It killed 64 people, collapsed Olive View hospital, and led to tougher building codes.
California earthquakes, in order.Loma Prieta: It struck during the World Series warm-up at Candlestick Park, and collapsed part of the Bay Bridge and a freeway.
California earthquakes, in order.Landers: It was magnitude 7.3 in the Mojave Desert, and it triggered smaller quakes as far away as Yellowstone.
California earthquakes, in order.Northridge: It struck at 4:31 in the morning in January and counts among the costliest US disasters.
California earthquakes, in order.South Napa: A magnitude 6.0 quake hit wine country in August, and was the strongest in the Bay Area since Loma Prieta.
California earthquakes, in order.Ridgecrest: A magnitude 6.4 foreshock was followed a day later by a 7.1, California's strongest in about 20 years.

Original Pokédex numbers.Bulbasaur: Number one in the Pokédex, a Grass and Poison type whose bulb grows on its back as it evolves. Its name blends bulb and dinosaur.
Original Pokédex numbers.Charmander: Its tail flame shows its health; the Pokédex says it dies if the flame goes out. It evolves into Charmeleon and then the dragon-like Charizard.
Original Pokédex numbers.Squirtle: This tiny turtle shoots water and retreats into its shell. In the first games it is one of the three starters, alongside Bulbasaur and Charmander.
Original Pokédex numbers.Pikachu: Nintendo's electric mouse became the franchise mascot, partly because of the anime. Its design was reportedly inspired by squirrels and the Japanese word for sparkle.
Original Pokédex numbers.Jigglypuff: A round, pink singer whose lullaby puts listeners to sleep. In the anime it gets furious when its audience dozes off and draws on their faces.
Original Pokédex numbers.Meowth: A cat that collects coins and appears in Team Rocket, where it famously speaks human language in the anime after learning by watching people.
Original Pokédex numbers.Gengar: A Ghost and Poison type said to hide in shadows and chill the room. In the games it is the final form of Gastly, reached through trading.
Original Pokédex numbers.Snorlax: This huge sleeper blocked roads in the original games until you played the Poké Flute. It can eat hundreds of kilograms of food a day.
Original Pokédex numbers.Mewtwo: A genetically engineered Pokémon cloned from Mew, and one of the strongest in the original games. It is number 150, just before the final entry.
Original Pokédex numbers.Mew: A secret Pokémon, number 151, added at the last minute by a programmer and kept out of the manual. Players could only get it through special events.

Animals in sayings, by real weight.Busy as a bee: A honeybee visits thousands of flowers a day, but over its entire lifetime it makes only about one twelfth of a teaspoon of honey.
Animals in sayings, by real weight.Blind as a bat: Bats are not blind; most can see quite well. They add echolocation so they can hunt flying insects in total darkness.
Animals in sayings, by real weight.Quiet as a mouse: Mice are not really silent, since they squeak at ultrasonic pitches humans cannot hear. They also sing to attract mates.
Animals in sayings, by real weight.Wise old owl: The reputation dates back to Athena, the Greek goddess of wisdom, whose symbol was an owl. In tests, owls are not especially clever, though their hunting skills are superb.
Animals in sayings, by real weight.Mad as a March hare: The saying comes from spring mating behaviour, when hares box and chase one another in fields. Females fend off pushy males by punching.
Animals in sayings, by real weight.Sly as a fox: Foxes have long been the cunning trickster in folk tales, from Aesop's fables onward. They are adaptable, and thrive in cities as well as countryside.
Animals in sayings, by real weight.Hungry as a wolf: A wolf can gulp down around 9 kg of meat at one meal. It may then go for days before the next kill.
Animals in sayings, by real weight.Like a bear with a sore head: The phrase refers to the grumpy temper of bears, and may date from bear-baiting days when captive bears were angered by dogs.
Animals in sayings, by real weight.Strong as an ox: Oxen are castrated male cattle trained to pull ploughs and carts. For thousands of years they were the tractors of farming.
Animals in sayings, by real weight.Elephant in the room: The idiom describes an obvious problem that everyone avoids discussing. An elephant is the largest land animal, so the image is hard to ignore.

Environmental milestones.Yellowstone becomes a park: The world's first national park was set aside to preserve its geysers and wildlife, an idea soon copied across the globe.
Environmental milestones.Sierra Club founded: Naturalist John Muir helped found this group in California, and it became one of the most influential US conservation organizations.
Environmental milestones.Silent Spring: Rachel Carson's book exposed the damage of pesticides like DDT on birds and helped launch the modern environmental movement.
Environmental milestones.Earthrise photo: Apollo 8 astronaut William Anders took this image of Earth over the Moon's horizon, and it changed how many people saw the planet.
Environmental milestones.First Earth Day: About 20 million Americans took part, and it helped spur laws such as the Clean Air Act and the founding of the EPA.
Environmental milestones.Blue Marble photo: Taken by Apollo 17's crew on their way to the Moon, this is one of the most reproduced photographs in history.
Environmental milestones.Montreal Protocol: This treaty phased out ozone-damaging chemicals and is often called one of the most successful environmental agreements ever.
Environmental milestones.Rio Earth Summit: This UN conference drew leaders from over a hundred countries and led to a climate convention that eventually produced later agreements.
Environmental milestones.Kyoto Protocol: The first treaty to set binding emission targets for rich nations, named for the Japanese city where it was agreed.
Environmental milestones.Paris Agreement: Nearly every country pledged to keep warming well below 2 degrees Celsius, with a goal of aiming for 1.5.
